verdicts.rewritten_summary: National-framework reporting (Washington Blade, 10 Apr 2025): President Milei eliminated the federal Women, Gender and Diversity Ministry, dismissed trans employees hired under the Trans Labour Quota Law (which reserved at least 1% of public-sector jobs for trans people), and on 5 Feb 2025 issued a decree restricting minors' access to gender-affirming surgery and hormone treatments. Argentine trans activists interviewed 4 Apr 2025 describe the community as facing a 'chaotic, desperate' situation with heightened exposure to violence, discrimination and poverty; the 2012 Gender Identity Law (legal gender change without medical gatekeeping) remains on the books. This national framework is what a trans visitor stands under in this Argentine province.
verdicts.note: national-framework reporting; record assessed at national score; no province-specific source

verdicts.rewritten_summary: National-framework report (Agencia Presentes, 19 Mar 2026) on the Observatorio Nacional de Crimenes de Odio LGBT+ figures: 2025 set a record with at least 227 bias-motivated crimes against LGBT people in Argentina (up on 2024), one every 38 hours; 62.5% of victims (142) were trans women or travestis, 18 trans men (vs 5 in 2024), 13 lesbians and 4 non-binary people; 64.8% (147 cases) were physical violence and 32% occurred in police stations or penal institutions, with police involvement jumping from 17 cases in 2024 to 64 in 2025. Frame applies to this province as part of the national position.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Case report (Association for Legal Intervention, 13 Mar 2024): a Polish regional court placed a transgender Vietnamese woman who had been on hormone therapy since 2018 in a guarded centre for male foreigners, and the Border Guard refused to move or release her despite Polish law barring placement wherever a stay would threaten life or health or the person shows signs of having suffered violence. After the association's application to the Border Guard Post commander she was released (page updated 28 Mar 2024). Establishes the current framework for trans foreigners in Polish immigration detention - directly relevant to any trans visitor detained while in this voivodeship.
verdicts.note: national-framework detention case; no voivodeship-specific source; rule 1 in-scope

verdicts.rewritten_summary: ECtHR ruling coverage (TGEU, 16 Jul 2024): on 11 Jul 2024 the European Court of Human Rights found Polish prison authorities violated a trans woman's right to private and family life (Article 8 ECHR) by denying her hormone-replacement therapy in Siedlce prison, awarding EUR 8,000 damages; the Court left the alleged Articles 3 and 14 breaches undecided but held the refusal had no reasonable legal grounds and was disproportionate. The judgment is binding on Poland as a whole - the governing standard for trans people's healthcare in Polish prisons and detention in every voivodeship, including this one.
verdicts.note: national ECtHR ruling binding on Poland; rule 1 in-scope
